title: Applications in industry: predictive maintenance, production and quality control

videos.script: A machine at Serra Azul ran for the whole of its shift. {{machine}} The light was green for eight hours. It still lost more than a quarter of the time it was meant to be making parts. It stopped twice. It ran slower than it should. And some of what it made went in the bin. {{oee}} One number counts all three losses, and this lesson takes it apart minute by minute. This is industry, read with the four questions of lesson 17. {{four}} The decisions are which machine makes what, when to stop one on purpose, and whether a batch can ship. {{chart}} You will see why a machine that fails often can look as good as one that hardly fails, and why one bad day is a signal while another is just noise. {{records}} And then the trap that belongs to factories. A machine counts every part it makes. A person writes down the scrap at the end of a long shift. Both numbers end up in the same table, and they do not agree.
